name: Tureenmead – Restaurant Online Ordering
author: Tico

sections.description:
Tureenmead finds the order buttons and menus GloriaFood left on your pages and, on your click, puts its own order button and menu in the same spots, so diners find the order button where it always was. Around that: online ordering on your own WordPress site with no WooCommerce and no cut of any order, pickup and delivery paid in person, an order screen that rings on a kitchen tablet until a person accepts, and your menu brought over with its sizes and add-ons by key or by file.

How Tureenmead is different

Your website moves with your menu. In the block and classic editor content of your pages, Tureenmead finds GloriaFood’s order buttons, menus, shortcodes and blocks, shows every page and every change before anything happens, and on your click puts its own order button and menu in the same spots. Elementor widgets, sidebar widgets and theme files are listed with the steps to change them by hand. Each changed page keeps a revision (or, on a page type without revisions, Tureenmead’s own copy) that one click puts back while the page is unchanged since.

Takeout orders and restaurant pickup

Diners open your menu on their phone, add dishes and choose pickup. They give a name and a phone number, an e-mail address if they want updates, and a time: as soon as possible, or a later time inside your opening hours, after the minutes your kitchen needs. They pay when they pick up, and a page of their own shows when the order is accepted and when it will be ready. Each takeout order arrives on your order screen with its pickup time.

Commission free online food ordering

There is no monthly fee, no commission and no cut of any order. Diners pay you in person, when they pick up or when the food arrives. Tureenmead needs no WooCommerce and asks you to make no account anywhere.

Food delivery by postcode

Turn on delivery and add your delivery zones: each zone is the postcodes you bring food to, with its own delivery fee, its least order and, if you like, an order total above which delivery is free. A diner who chooses delivery types an address and a postcode; the postcode is checked against your zones and the fee is added to the order. No map is used, and no address leaves your site.

A kitchen display that rings: the order screen for restaurants

Open Tureenmead › Orders on a tablet in the kitchen and tap Start taking orders. Each new order rings until a person presses Accept, with the minutes it needs, or Refuse, saying why; the diner’s own page then shows the answer. An order that waits past the minutes you set turns red with a harsher sound, and one e-mail about it goes to your order address while the order screen or the diner’s page is open. Print ticket prints an order for a receipt printer or an A4 page, and more than one tablet can take orders at once. Each ticket marks a regular with the orders they placed before.

Your restaurant menu: sizes, add-ons and allergens

Build your menu on Tureenmead › Menu: categories in the order diners see them, and in each one its dishes, each with a price, a photo from your Media Library, a description, its allergens and nutrition as you would tell a diner, and marks such as spicy, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free or halal. A dish can come in sizes, each with its own price, and carry groups of extras a diner picks from, like a sauce or toppings, with the least and most picks you set. Mark a dish “Sold out today” and it is back on sale when you next open; hide a dish or a whole category without deleting it. Show the menu on any page with the Menu and order block or the [tureenmead_menu] shortcode, and an order button anywhere with the Order button block or [tureenmead_order_button].

Your orders and customers

Every order is in one list, newest first, filtered by day, status, pickup or delivery, and searched by order number, name or phone, with a line for the day: orders received, accepted, refused and waiting, and any the order limits turned away. The customers list is built from your orders, with how many times each person ordered and when last. Your regulars can come across from your own spreadsheet too: choose its CSV file, match its columns to name, phone, e-mail, orders before and May we e-mail you, see the first 5 people as they will be kept, and import them; the file itself is not kept, and importing the same file twice adds nobody twice. Both download as a CSV file for a spreadsheet. Deleting a customer removes their name and contact details from their past orders and keeps the totals.

Bring your menu over

Your GloriaFood menu comes over with its sizes, add-ons and groups, by the Fetch Menu key from its admin or by the menu file. The key is used once and never stored. Dish photos are added from your Media Library.

GloriaFood is a trademark of its owner. Tureenmead is not affiliated with or endorsed by it.

External services

Tureenmead calls one outside address, pos.globalfoodsoft.com, the menu address of GloriaFood’s Fetch Menu, and only when you press Import my menu on Tureenmead › Import with your own Fetch Menu key. It sends that key, and the name Tureenmead with its version as the program asking; your menu comes back, with its categories, dishes, sizes, add-ons and prices. It is never called by itself, on a schedule or by a diner, and the key is used for that one request and never stored. The import by key works only while GloriaFood’s server answers; the import by menu file calls no outside address.

GloriaFood’s own words, on https://www.gloriafood.com/ (read 2026-11-04): “GloriaFood will reach end of life on April 30, 2027.”

  • What the address returns, in GloriaFood’s documentation: https://github.com/GlobalFood/integration_docs/blob/master/fetch_menu/README.md
  • Terms of Use: https://www.gloriafood.com/terms-of-use
  • The agreement a restaurant accepts for its account: https://www.globalfoodsoft.com/api/legal?type=eula_restaurants
  • Privacy policy: https://www.oracle.com/legal/privacy/oracle-restaurants-estore-privacy-policy/

Privacy

Each order’s name, phone, e-mail, address and note are kept in your own site’s database, and nowhere else. The diner’s own order page is opened by a long random link and never shows the name, phone, e-mail or address. Order e-mails are sent by your site’s own mail.

You choose how long a diner’s details stay on their orders: 90 days, 180 days, a year (the default), 2 years, or until you delete them. After that, a daily clear blanks the name, phone, e-mail, address and notes; the dishes and totals stay for your accounts. If your site’s scheduled tasks do not run, the clear runs the next time you open a Tureenmead screen.

Tools › Export Personal Data and Tools › Erase Personal Data include Tureenmead’s orders and customers list. Settings › Privacy offers suggested text for your privacy policy, which follows your choice. It is not legal advice.
sections.faq:
Do diners pay online?

Not in this version. Diners pay you in person, when they pick up their order or when the food arrives; there are no online card payments in this version. What they read at checkout about paying is yours to word in Settings › Orders › “How diners pay, in your words”.

Is there a monthly fee or a cut of each order?

No. There is no fee, no commission and no cut of any order, however many orders you take.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Tureenmead takes orders on its own. On a site that runs WooCommerce, Tureenmead works beside it and changes nothing of it.

What does the kitchen tablet need?

The order screen (Tureenmead › Orders) open in its browser, signed in as you or as an order taker, the tablet plugged in with its sound on, and one tap on Start taking orders each time the screen is opened: a browser plays a sound only after a tap on its page. Where the browser allows it, the screen keeps the tablet awake while it is open; where it does not, the screen says so and you set the tablet never to sleep while it is plugged in. An iPad, an Android tablet or a laptop all work, either way up.

Does Tureenmead ever turn an order away?

Only a flood of orders. One address can place 5 orders in 10 minutes. The next order from there is asked to try again in the minutes left, or to call the restaurant. The whole site takes 20 new orders in one minute; the next one in that minute reads “We are taking a lot of orders right now. Please try again in a minute, or call us.” Each order a limit turns away is counted in the day’s line on Tureenmead › Order list. Your own test orders never count toward either limit. If your host or a proxy in front of your site hands WordPress one address for every visitor, all your diners share the first limit: ask your host to pass each visitor’s own address on to WordPress.

What if nobody accepts an order?

The order screen keeps ringing until a person accepts or refuses it. Once an order has waited the minutes set in Settings › Orders › “Minutes before an order that waits is mailed to you” (5 unless you change them), the screen turns red, the ring becomes a harsher sound, and one e-mail about that order goes to Settings › Orders › “Where new orders are mailed” (your site’s own address unless you type another) — sent while the order screen, or the diner’s own order page, is open. It cannot ring a tablet that is muted, asleep, out of power or offline, or one with the order screen closed. When the screen is signed out, offline or cannot reach your site, a red banner across the top says which, with a sound, until it is fixed. Each answer from your site keeps the screen signed in through a long shift.

How do I set up online ordering?

The Orders screen opens with a short checklist: start your menu with one dish or bring it over, put the order button on your pages or make a Menu & Order page, and place a test order on your own page as a diner would. The test order rings on the Orders screen, you accept it, and the diner’s page changes; it is left out of every count. The steps go away with your first real order.

How do I check that the tablet rings?

Tap Test the sound to hear the ring once. Place a test order makes an order that rings like a real one; it is marked as a test, never mailed to anyone and left out of every count. Once a published page shows your menu, its ticket has a link, See it as the diner sees it, that opens the page a diner would have: it says the order waits, and changes when you accept or refuse it.

Can more than one tablet take orders at once?

Yes. Both ring; the first Accept or Refuse wins, and the other tablet says who answered.

Can I print an order?

Yes. Print ticket prints the open order on its own, sized for a receipt printer (80 mm) or an A4 page, through the browser’s own print.

Where do the ring sounds come from?

They are Tureenmead’s own, made from plain tones, and ship with the plugin under the GPL. The screen fetches no sound from the internet.

How do delivery zones work?

In Settings › Delivery zones, each zone is a list of postcodes you type, with its own fee, its least order and, if you like, an order total above which delivery is free. A postcode ending in * covers every postcode that starts with it, and a postcode in more than one zone gets the lower fee. There is no map: the diner’s postcode is all that is checked. A US ZIP+4 a diner types matches the ZIP it starts with. Delivery is offered once Settings › Taking orders › “You deliver” is ticked and a zone has its postcodes. To take a zone away, tick its “Remove this zone” box and save.

How do opening hours, closed days and tax work?

In Settings › Opening hours you set each day’s hours in your site’s time zone, with a lunch and a dinner if you like; a closing time earlier than the opening runs past midnight. Diners can only choose a pickup or delivery time inside your hours, after the minutes your kitchen needs. Holidays and other closed days come before the hours, and Settings › Taking orders › “Pause new orders” stops new orders, with your own words to diners. In Settings › Tax and currency, tax is either in your prices or added to each order as its own line, on the delivery fee too if you choose. Prices are never converted between currencies.

What does a diner see after ordering?

A page of their own with the order number, the dishes and the total. It says when the restaurant accepts the order and when it will be ready, or why it was refused, and the diner gets the same news by e-mail if they gave an address.

Can I bring my menu over?

Yes, on Tureenmead › Import: by the Fetch Menu key from your old ordering system’s admin, or by its menu file (its name ends in .json, 5 MB at most). Sizes, add-on groups and their choices come too, and you see the menu before anything is added. Photos are added from your Media Library. Bringing it over again updates what the last import made and never touches dishes you made yourself.

What happens when the old ordering service closes?

The import by key works only while that service’s server answers; its end-of-life date is under External services, in its own words. The import by menu file, Tureenmead’s own order buttons and everything else keep working, because your menu and your orders are on your own site.

What does the order-buttons swap change?

Only the pages you tick, and only after you have seen each change on the Order buttons screen. The old order button or menu is replaced like for like in the same spot and the rest of the page stays as it was; table booking buttons and opening hours are left as they are and listed. It never changes another plugin or its settings. Elementor widgets, sidebar widgets and theme files are listed with the steps to change them by hand. If no page shows your menu yet, Tureenmead makes a Menu & Order page first for your order buttons to open. Each changed page keeps a revision that one click, Put it back, restores while the page is unchanged since.

Can I bring my customer list?

Yes, on Tureenmead › Customers: choose a CSV file of your own and match its columns to name, phone, e-mail, orders before and May we e-mail you. Only those are kept, never the file itself, and the order screen then marks your regulars. Importing sends nobody any mail.

Does it work with a page cache?

Yes. The menu page is the same for every diner; the cart asks your site for a fresh form when it opens.

What happens to my menu page if I delete Tureenmead?

Settings › Keeping diners’ details lists, under If Tureenmead is deleted, every page that shows Tureenmead’s menu or order button: once Tureenmead is deleted, its block there shows nothing and its shortcode shows as plain text, like [tureenmead_menu]. The pages its order-button swap changed can be put back from there first, with Put them all back. Deleting Tureenmead removes its own tables, settings and role, unless you tick “Keep my orders and customers if Tureenmead is deleted”: then the orders and the customers list stay. Your pages, your theme and your other plugins stay as they are.

What can I change, and where?

Everything is on Tureenmead › Settings, in these cards:

  • Taking orders: “Pause new orders”, with “What diners read while orders are paused”; “Diners can pick up their order” (on) and “Minutes until a pickup order is ready” (20); “You deliver” (off) and “Minutes until a delivery arrives” (45); “Times diners can choose” (every 15 minutes); “How far ahead diners can order” (today and tomorrow).
  • Opening hours: each day’s opening and closing times, with a lunch and a dinner if you like, and “Closed days” for holidays.
  • Delivery zones: each zone’s “Name”, “Postcodes, separated by commas”, “Delivery fee”, “Least order for delivery” and “Free delivery from an order of”.
  • Tax and currency: “My prices include tax” (the default) or “Add tax to each order, as its own line”; “Tax rate, in percent”; “Add tax to the delivery fee too” (off); “Currency (its three-letter code)” (USD); “Currency sign”; “Where the sign goes”.
  • Orders: “Where new orders are mailed” (your site’s own address unless you type another); “Minutes before an order that waits is mailed to you” (5); “How diners pay, in your words”.
  • Your diners’ page: “The order button’s words” (Order online unless you type your own); “Your phone number”, shown to diners who need to phone you.
  • Keeping diners’ details: “Clear diners’ names, phones, e-mails, addresses and notes from orders older than” (1 year); “Keep my orders and customers if Tureenmead is deleted” (off).
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First version: your menu with sizes, add-ons and allergens; pickup and delivery paid in person, with delivery zones by postcode and your opening hours; an order screen that rings on a kitchen tablet until a person accepts; the diner’s own order page; your orders and customers lists; your menu brought over by key or by file.
  • What makes Tureenmead different: it finds the order buttons, shortcodes and blocks of the hosted ordering service its menu-key import connects to and, on your click, puts its own order button in each same spot, every changed page kept so you can put it back.

A dish with sizes and add-ons. The price on the Add button grows with each pick, and the cart shows every choice.
The order screen on a kitchen tablet rings for each new order until someone accepts or refuses it. Tap Accept, then the minutes it needs.
The diner's own order page: waiting for the restaurant, then accepted, with about when it will be ready.
